query: what makes dirt good for growing crops

payload.answer: Dirt is good for growing crops when it contains sufficient plant nutrients and moisture. For example, black soil is rich in nutrients like calcium carbonate, magnesium, potash, and lime, and its clayey texture helps it hold moisture well [2]. Similarly, alluvial soils found on river terraces are fertile because they contain various proportions of sand, silt, and clay that support growth [2]. In contrast, laterite soil can be very useful for crops like tea and coffee if proper conservation techniques are used to prevent erosion and manage its nutrient deficiencies [1].
